questions.questionText: Which feature best helps the pictured nerve cell carry signals over long distances?
options: Its lack of a cell membrane
questions.explanation: The extended fibre allows electrical impulses to travel between distant parts of the body.

curriculum.objective: Relate specialised cell structures to functions and explain organisation in living systems.

questions.questionText: Which sequence shows increasing biological organisation?
questions.explanation: Similar cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs cooperate in systems.

curriculum.objective: Relate specialised cell structures to functions and explain organisation in living systems.

questions.questionText: Why are root hair cells effective at absorbing water and minerals?
options: Their projections provide a large surface area
questions.correctAnswer: Their projections provide a large surface area
questions.explanation: The hair-like projection increases contact with soil water and dissolved mineral ions.

curriculum.objective: Relate specialised cell structures to functions and explain organisation in living systems.

questions.questionText: During vigorous exercise, why do breathing rate and heart rate both increase?
options: To cool the bones inside joints
To reduce blood flow to muscles
To supply more oxygen and remove more carbon dioxide
questions.correctAnswer: To supply more oxygen and remove more carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Working muscles respire faster, requiring increased oxygen delivery and carbon dioxide removal.

curriculum.objective: Relate specialised cell structures to functions and explain organisation in living systems.

questions.questionText: What process causes the particles to become evenly distributed?
questions.explanation: Random particle motion causes net movement from high to low concentration until distribution is even.

curriculum.objective: Use particle models and conservation to explain diffusion, reactions and separation processes.

questions.questionText: Which word equation matches the particle model?
questions.explanation: The diagram shows two AB units plus one B₂ unit forming two AB₂ units.

curriculum.objective: Use particle models and conservation to explain diffusion, reactions and separation processes.

questions.questionText: Which method best separates pure water from a salt solution?
questions.explanation: Distillation boils and condenses the water while the dissolved salt remains behind.

curriculum.objective: Use particle models and conservation to explain diffusion, reactions and separation processes.

questions.questionText: A sealed flask has a mass of 145.6 g before a reaction. What mass should it have after the reaction?
options: More than 145.6 g in every case
questions.explanation: In a closed system atoms are rearranged but not lost, so total mass is conserved.

curriculum.objective: Use particle models and conservation to explain diffusion, reactions and separation processes.

questions.questionText: During which interval is the object stationary?
questions.explanation: A horizontal distance–time segment means distance is unchanged, so the object is stationary.

curriculum.objective: Interpret motion graphs and apply resultant force and pressure relationships.

questions.questionText: Which position produces the greater pressure on the surface?
questions.explanation: The same weight acts through a smaller contact area in B, producing greater pressure.

curriculum.objective: Interpret motion graphs and apply resultant force and pressure relationships.

questions.questionText: A runner travels 150 m in 30 s. What is the average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed is distance divided by time: 150 ÷ 30 = 5 m/s.

curriculum.objective: Interpret motion graphs and apply resultant force and pressure relationships.

questions.questionText: A 12 N force acts right and a 7 N force acts left on a 2 kg cart. What motion change should result?
options: The cart accelerates to the left
The cart accelerates to the right
questions.correctAnswer: The cart accelerates to the right
questions.explanation: The resultant is 5 N to the right, so the cart accelerates in that direction.

curriculum.objective: Interpret motion graphs and apply resultant force and pressure relationships.

questions.questionText: What happens to the other lamp if one lamp is removed from this parallel circuit?
options: It can remain lit on its own branch
It always goes out because there is one path
It receives no electrical energy in any circuit
questions.correctAnswer: It can remain lit on its own branch
questions.explanation: Each parallel branch provides a separate complete path, so the other branch can keep working.

curriculum.objective: Analyse circuit behaviour and quantify useful and dissipated energy transfers.

questions.questionText: How much energy is transferred as thermal energy in the diagram?
questions.explanation: Energy is conserved, so thermal transfer is 100 J input minus 20 J light = 80 J.

curriculum.objective: Analyse circuit behaviour and quantify useful and dissipated energy transfers.

questions.questionText: Which device transfers electrical energy mainly into kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: A fan motor uses electrical energy to produce movement of its blades.

curriculum.objective: Analyse circuit behaviour and quantify useful and dissipated energy transfers.

questions.questionText: A machine receives 500 J and transfers 350 J usefully. What is its efficiency?
questions.explanation: Efficiency is useful output divided by input: 350/500 × 100% = 70%.

curriculum.objective: Analyse circuit behaviour and quantify useful and dissipated energy transfers.

questions.questionText: What is the independent variable in the pictured investigation?
questions.explanation: The deliberately changed factor is temperature; the other shown conditions are controlled.

curriculum.objective: Design fair investigations, analyse patterns and evaluate reliability, validity and conclusions.

questions.questionText: Why should each dissolving test be repeated?
options: To identify variation and calculate a representative mean
To guarantee the prediction is correct
questions.correctAnswer: To identify variation and calculate a representative mean
questions.explanation: Repeats reveal random variation and allow a mean that better represents the result.

curriculum.objective: Design fair investigations, analyse patterns and evaluate reliability, validity and conclusions.

questions.questionText: A result lies far from all repeats and a procedural mistake was recorded. What is the best action?
options: Change the hypothesis to match it
Repeat that trial and justify excluding the anomalous result
Average it twice so it has more influence
questions.correctAnswer: Repeat that trial and justify excluding the anomalous result
questions.explanation: A documented procedural error supports a transparent repeat and justified treatment of the anomaly.

curriculum.objective: Design fair investigations, analyse patterns and evaluate reliability, validity and conclusions.

questions.questionText: Two variables rise together in an observational study. Which conclusion is safest?
options: One variable certainly causes the other
They are associated, but the study alone does not prove causation
questions.correctAnswer: They are associated, but the study alone does not prove causation
questions.explanation: Correlation supports an association, while uncontrolled factors may explain the pattern.

curriculum.objective: Design fair investigations, analyse patterns and evaluate reliability, validity and conclusions.
